questions.question: What is the primary architectural advantage of CSS Container Queries over standard Media Queries?
options: Container queries allow components to adapt based on the size of their parent container rather than the entire browser viewport
Container queries only work on Linux servers
Container queries compile CSS to WebGL
questions.hint: Responsive adaptation based on parent container width.
questions.explanation: Container queries inspect the dimensions of the immediate parent container, enabling truly modular, reusable UI components.

questions.question: Which property must be declared on a parent element to establish a container context for width queries?
questions.explanation: container-type: inline-size establishes a containment context on the element's inline axis (width).

questions.question: What does the container query unit 'cqw' represent?
questions.explanation: 1cqw represents 1% of the query container's width, analogous to 1vw for viewports.

questions.question: If a card component is placed inside a 300px sidebar on a 4K desktop monitor, how does @container (min-width: 500px) evaluate?
options: It evaluates to true because the monitor is 4K
It evaluates to false because the container is only 300px wide
questions.explanation: Container queries look at the container size (300px); since 300px is less than 500px, the query evaluates to false.

questions.question: Which at-rule initiates a container query block in modern CSS?
questions.explanation: @container (min-width: ...) is the standard syntax for container queries in CSS.
